Whenever late_fee charges a fee, it charges 2% of amount_cents for each started 30-day period of days_late (6 to 30 days is one period, 31 to 60 is two, and so on), and a fractional days_late counts as a started period.
Whenever the computed late_fee is not a whole number of cents, it rounds the fee up to the next whole cent.
Whenever the computed late_fee is below 500 cents, it is raised to a minimum of 500 cents.

Whenever late_fee would exceed one fifth (20%) of amount_cents, it is limited to amount_cents divided by 5, rounded down to a whole cent; this cap is applied after the minimum, so on a small invoice the cap wins over the 500-cent minimum.
Whenever make_slug receives a title or maxlen that is NULL or (for maxlen) not a number, it returns NULL.
Whenever make_slug builds a slug, it lowercases the title and replaces every ampersand with the word 'and'.

Whenever the title contains the whole words 'the', 'a', 'an' or 'of', make_slug drops them from the slug; words that merely contain them, such as 'another', stay.
Whenever make_slug joins the remaining words, it joins them with a single hyphen, with no leading or trailing hyphen.

Whenever the slug is longer than maxlen, make_slug cuts it at maxlen characters; if the cut falls in the middle of a word and the kept part contains a hyphen, it backs up to the last hyphen so no partial word remains.
Whenever the cut falls exactly at the end of a word, make_slug keeps that whole word without backing up.
Whenever the cut falls in the middle of the first word (no hyphen in the kept part), make_slug keeps the partial word cut at maxlen characters.
Whenever make_slug cuts a slug, it removes any hyphens left at the ends of the result.
Whenever maxlen is negative, make_slug treats it as 0, and a fractional maxlen is truncated toward zero to a whole number.
Whenever the resulting slug is empty (empty or blank title, a title of only punctuation or stopwords, or maxlen of 0 or less), make_slug returns the text 'untitled'.
Whenever make_slug receives a non-text, non-NULL title, it converts it to text first.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives NULL or a non-number, it returns NULL.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives negative points, it returns 'suspended'.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives points from 0 up to but not including 1000, it returns 'bronze'; zero is bronze.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives points from 1000 up to but not including 5000, it returns 'silver'.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives points from 5000 up to but not including 20000, it returns 'gold'.
Whenever loyalty_tier receives 20000 points or more, it returns 'platinum', with no further tier above it; each lower bound belongs to the higher tier, and fractional points are compared as they are.
Whenever fiscal_label receives NULL, it returns NULL.

Whenever fiscal_label receives text that is not a date in YYYY-MM-DD form (empty text, other layouts, free text, a non-text value), it returns the text 'INVALID'; leading and trailing whitespace is ignored first.
Whenever fiscal_label receives a date that does not exist on the calendar (month 13, day 45, 29 February in a non-leap year, year 0000), it returns 'INVALID'.

Whenever isbn_check receives NULL, it returns NULL; any other value is converted to text first.
Whenever isbn_check reads the code, it ignores every character that is not a digit 0-9 (hyphens, spaces, letters).
Whenever the code holds more than 9 digits, isbn_check uses only the first 9 digits and ignores the rest.
Whenever isbn_check computes the check digit, it multiplies the first digit by 1, the second by 2, and so on up to the ninth by 9, adds the products, and takes the sum modulo 11.
Whenever the isbn_check remainder is 10, it returns the letter 'X'; otherwise it returns the remainder as one digit of text.

Whenever meeting_end receives a start or minutes that is NULL, or minutes that is not a number, it returns NULL.

Whenever meeting_end receives a start that is not exactly two-digit hours, a colon and two-digit minutes (such as '9:00', or text), or has hours above 23 or minutes above 59, it returns NULL; surrounding whitespace is ignored.

Whenever meeting_end receives minutes of zero or less, it adds nothing and returns the start time itself.
Whenever the end time would pass 23:59, meeting_end returns '23:59'; bookings never wrap past midnight into the next day, and reaching 24:00 exactly also gives '23:59'.
Whenever meeting_end returns a time, it is written HH:MM with two digits for each part.
Whenever pct_change receives a NULL or non-number old or new, it returns NULL.
Whenever pct_change receives an old value of zero, it returns 0.0 whatever the new value is (no division by zero, no NULL).

Whenever phone_fmt receives NULL, it returns NULL; any other value is converted to text first.
Whenever phone_fmt reads the input, it ignores every character that is not a digit 0-9 (spaces, dashes, dots, brackets, plus signs, letters, extension text) and counts the digits that remain.
Whenever the input holds exactly 10 digits, phone_fmt returns them as '(AAA) EEE-NNNN'.

Whenever the input holds any other number of digits (fewer or more than 10, including 11 digits with a leading 1, an extension, or none), phone_fmt returns the original text unchanged, without trimming or changing it.

Whenever avg_rating runs over a group, it ignores values that are NULL, not numbers (text, boolean), or outside the range 1 to 5 inclusive; 1 and 5 themselves count, and fractional ratings such as 4.5 count.
Whenever no valid ratings remain in the group (empty group, all NULL, or all out of range), avg_rating returns NULL.
Whenever avg_rating has 5 or more valid ratings, it drops exactly one lowest and one highest rating before averaging; when values tie for lowest or highest, only one copy of each is dropped.
Whenever avg_rating has fewer than 5 valid ratings, it drops nothing and averages them all.
Whenever avg_rating computes the average, it rounds to 1 decimal with an exact half rounding up (3.25 gives 3.3), computed on the exact decimal values, and returns it as a decimal number.

Whenever bulk_price is given a quantity of 50 or more, it takes 10% off the whole order, so 50 units at 100 cents cost 4500.
Whenever a bulk_price discount leaves a fraction of a cent, bulk_price rounds half a cent up to the next whole cent (15 cents x 10 units gives 143, 3 x 10 gives 29).
Whenever bulk_price is given a quantity of zero or less, or a negative unit price, it returns 0 rather than a negative or error value.
Whenever either input to bulk_price is NULL, empty text, or any text (even '100' or '5'), bulk_price returns NULL; only real numbers are accepted, and this check comes before the zero/negative rule.
Whenever bulk_price is given a fractional quantity or price and no discount applies, it drops the fraction of the total (10.5 cents x 3 gives 31, 100 x 9.99 gives 999, while 100 x 2.5 gives 250).

Whenever bulk_price is given a fractional quantity of 10 or more or a fractional unit price with a discount, the discount tier is judged on the exact quantity (10.5 counts as 10 or more) and the discounted total is rounded half up, though it may come back in decimal form such as 998.0.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice that is 30 days late or fewer (including zero or negative days), the fee is 0.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice that is 31 to 60 days late, the fee is 4% of the invoice amount.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice that is 61 or more days late, the fee is 6% of the whole invoice amount, not in addition to the 4%.
Whenever a late_fee percentage leaves a fraction of a cent, late_fee rounds half a cent up, so 4% of 12 cents is 0 and 4% of 13 cents is 1; small invoices can therefore owe no fee.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice amount of zero or less, the fee is 0, whatever the days late.

Whenever late_fee is given a fractional days_late, it applies the same limits to the exact value (30.5 days is already in the 4% band, 60.5 days in the 6% band), and a fractional amount gives a whole-cent fee (100.5 cents at 4% gives 4).
Whenever either input to late_fee is NULL, empty text or text of any kind (even '1000' or '40'), late_fee returns NULL, even when the amount is zero or the days are negative.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given fewer than 1000 points, it returns 'bronze'; this includes 0, negative balances and 999.9.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given 1000 to 4999 points (4999.5 included), it returns 'silver'; exactly 1000 is silver.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given 5000 points or more, it returns 'gold'; exactly 5000 is gold.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given NULL, empty text or any text (even '5000'), it returns NULL.

Whenever make_slug is given a title, it lowercases it and turns every run of characters that are not English letters a-z or digits 0-9 (spaces, punctuation, underscores, slashes, hyphens) into a single hyphen, and removes hyphens from the start and end ('  Hello,   World!! ' becomes 'hello-world').

Whenever a title contains accented or non-English letters, make_slug does not transliterate them but treats them as separators ('Café Crème' becomes 'caf-cr-me'), and a title with no a-z or digits at all, or an empty title, gives empty text.
Whenever make_slug is given a maxlen, it cuts the slug to at most that many characters and then removes any hyphen left at the end ('Hello World' with maxlen 6 gives 'hello', with 1 gives 'h').

Whenever make_slug is given a maxlen of zero or less, empty text, or text that is not a number, it returns empty text; a numeric text such as '5' works as 5 and a fractional maxlen such as 5.9 is cut down to 5.
Whenever make_slug is given a NULL maxlen, it applies no length limit; a NULL title returns NULL whatever the maxlen.
Whenever make_slug is given a number as the title, it uses the number's text (12345 becomes '12345', 1.5 becomes '1-5').

Whenever isbn_check is given exactly 9 digits, it multiplies the digits by 10, 9, 8 ... 2 from left to right, adds them, and returns the digit that brings the total to a multiple of 11; if that digit would be 10 it returns 'X'; the result is text ('030640615' gives '2', '123456789' gives 'X', '000000000' gives '0').
Whenever isbn_check is given a code with leading or trailing spaces around 9 digits, it ignores those outer spaces; spaces or hyphens inside the code make it invalid.
Whenever isbn_check is given anything other than exactly 9 ASCII digits (8 or 10 digits, letters including an X, hyphens, empty text, non-Western digits, or NULL), it returns NULL.

Whenever isbn_check is given a whole number of 9 digits (123456789), it treats it as text and works; a number with fewer digits (30640615, which has lost its leading zero) or a decimal such as 30640615.0 returns NULL, with no leading zero added.
Whenever fiscal_label is given a valid YYYY-MM-DD date, the fiscal year starts on 1 April and is named for the calendar year it ends in, so 2024-04-01 is 'FY2025-Q1' and 2025-03-31 is 'FY2025-Q4'.

Whenever fiscal_label is given a date, quarters run Q1 April-June, Q2 July-September, Q3 October-December and Q4 January-March, so 2024-06-30 is Q1, 2024-07-01 is Q2, 2024-10-01 is Q3 and 2025-01-01 is Q4; the label looks like 'FY2025-Q1'.
Whenever fiscal_label is given a date that does not exist (2024-02-30, 2023-02-29, month 13, month 00), it returns NULL, while a real leap day such as 2024-02-29 is accepted and labelled 'FY2024-Q4'.

Whenever fiscal_label is given text not in the exact form of four-digit year, two-digit month and two-digit day separated by hyphens (2024-1-5, 2024/04/01, 20240401, a date with a time, empty text, a number, or NULL), it returns NULL; spaces around a valid date are ignored.
Whenever fiscal_label is given an extreme year, it still applies the same rule without a range check: year 0001 gives 'FY2-Q1' with no zero padding, and 9999-12-31 gives 'FY10000-Q3'.

Whenever meeting_end is given a start time and a number of minutes, it returns the start plus those minutes as HH:MM on the 24-hour clock with zero padding ('09:00' plus 60 gives '10:00', '9:05' plus 30 gives '09:35').

Whenever a booking runs past midnight, meeting_end wraps around to the next day's clock time without saying so ('23:30' plus 60 gives '00:30', 1440 minutes gives the same time back, 1500 minutes adds one hour).
Whenever meeting_end is given negative minutes, it counts backwards from the start and wraps to the previous evening if needed ('10:00' minus 30 gives '09:30', '00:10' minus 30 gives '23:40').

Whenever meeting_end is given a start that is not H:MM or HH:MM with two-digit minutes (24:00, 12:60, '9am', '09:00:00', '9:5', empty text, a number, or NULL), it returns NULL; one or two digit hours and spaces around the start are accepted.
Whenever meeting_end is given NULL minutes, it returns NULL.

Whenever meeting_end is given minutes with a fraction, it drops the fraction toward zero (45.9 gives 45 minutes, -45.9 gives -45); numeric text such as '30' or '1e2' is read as a number, text that begins with a number ('30 min') uses that number, and text with no leading number or empty text counts as 0 minutes.

Whenever pct_change is given an old and a new value, it returns (new minus old) divided by the size of old, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal, as a decimal number: 100 to 150 is 50.0 and 150 to 100 is -33.3.
Whenever pct_change is given a negative old value, it divides by the old value's size without its sign, so a rise reads as positive (-100 to -50 is 50.0, -100 to 50 is 150.0).
Whenever pct_change is given an old value of 0, it returns NULL; a new value of 0 gives -100.0, and no change gives 0.0.
Whenever pct_change is given a NULL for either value, it returns NULL.

Whenever pct_change is given numeric text such as '100' or ' 100 ', it uses the number; text that does not start with a number or is empty counts as 0, so an old value of that kind gives NULL and a new value of that kind gives -100.0; text starting with a number ('150abc') uses the leading number.
Whenever pct_change is given a binary (blob) value for either side, it returns NULL.

Whenever the pct_change result falls exactly halfway at the second decimal, it rounds away from zero (2000 to 2001 gives 0.1, 2000 to 1999 gives -0.1), but values that are only a hair below the halfway point because of decimal inexactness round down (100 to 100.05 gives 0.0).

Whenever phone_fmt is given a phone number with 10 digits, it ignores every non-digit character (brackets, hyphens, dots, spaces, plus sign, even letters or surrounding words) and returns it as (AAA) EEE-NNNN ('212.555.1234' and 'call 212-555-1234 now' both give '(212) 555-1234').

Whenever phone_fmt finds 11 digits and the first is 1, it drops that leading 1 as the country code and formats the remaining 10 ('+1 212 555 1234' gives '(212) 555-1234'); 11 digits starting with any other digit are not formatted.

Whenever phone_fmt is given anything with some other count of digits (7, 9, 12 digits, no digits, empty text, an international number like '+44 20 7946 0958', or non-Western digits), it returns the input exactly as it was given.
Whenever phone_fmt is given NULL, it returns NULL.

Whenever phone_fmt is given a whole number of 10 digits (2125551234) or 11 digits starting with 1, it formats it as text, but a number with a decimal point (2125551234.0) or one with too few digits is returned unchanged as a number.
Whenever phone_fmt is given 10 digits, it does not check that the area code or exchange is valid, so '0125551234' gives '(012) 555-1234' and '0000000000' gives '(000) 000-0000'.
Whenever avg_rating is applied to a group of rows, it returns the plain average of the ratings between 1 and 5 inclusive, with no rounding (ratings 4 and 5 give 4.5, and 5, 3, 1, 2.5 give 2.875).
Whenever a row's rating is NULL, below 1, above 5, or text (even '4'), avg_rating leaves it out of the average completely, counting neither its value nor the row.
Whenever a group has no ratings that count (no rows, all NULL, empty text, or all outside 1 to 5), avg_rating returns NULL.

Whenever avg_rating is used with GROUP BY, it gives one average per group, and without GROUP BY it averages across all selected rows; it is not available on a single value outside a group of rows (avg_rating(5) gives NULL).

A January 2026 sale counts in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while a December 2026 sale counts in fiscal 2027.
A sale dated 30 February 2026, which does not exist, gets no label at all rather than an error.
A sale stamped 1 April 2026 at 10:00 with the time of day attached gets no label, so timestamps must be trimmed to a plain date first.
For catalogue code 123456789 the check character is the letter X, not a digit.
Catalogue code 0-306-40615 typed with hyphens gets no check digit, even though it holds the same nine digits as 030640615, which gets 2.
A catalogue code with only 8 digits gets no check digit instead of an error.
Spaces around catalogue code 030640615 are ignored, so it still gets the check digit 2.
An empty catalogue code gets no check digit.
The page 'Hello World Today' with an 8-character limit is cut in the middle of a word and becomes 'hello-wo'.
The product 'Café Crème' loses its accented letters and becomes 'caf-cr-me', with the accents turned into dashes.
A product titled '日本語 shoes' is reduced to just 'shoes', because non-English letters are dropped entirely.
The page 'Hello World' with a length limit of 0 gets an empty address, and a negative limit does the same.

Sales that grew from 0 to 50 units show no percentage change at all, because there is nothing to compare against.

rules: Whenever bulk_price is given a unit price and a quantity of fewer than 10, it returns unit price times quantity with no discount.
Whenever bulk_price is given a quantity of 10 to 49, it takes 5% off the whole order (not just the units above 10), so 10 units at 100 cents cost 950.

Whenever bulk_price is given a quantity of 100 or more, it takes 15% off the whole order. When it is given a quantity of 50 to 99, it takes 10% off the whole order, so 50 units at 100 cents cost 4500.
Whenever a bulk_price discount leaves a fraction of a cent, bulk_price rounds half a cent up to the next whole cent (15 cents x 10 units gives 143, 3 x 10 gives 29).
Whenever bulk_price is given a quantity of zero or less, or a negative unit price, it returns 0 rather than a negative or error value.
Whenever either input to bulk_price is NULL, empty text, or any text (even '100' or '5'), bulk_price returns NULL; only real numbers are accepted, and this check comes before the zero/negative rule.
Whenever bulk_price is given a fractional quantity or price and no discount applies, it drops the fraction of the total (10.5 cents x 3 gives 31, 100 x 9.99 gives 999, while 100 x 2.5 gives 250).

Whenever bulk_price is given a fractional quantity of 10 or more or a fractional unit price with a discount, the discount tier is judged on the exact quantity (10.5 counts as 10 or more) and the discounted total is rounded half up, though it may come back in decimal form such as 998.0.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice that is 30 days late or fewer (including zero or negative days), the fee is 0.

Rule 10: Whenever late_fee is given an invoice, the fee is 2% of the invoice amount per started 30-day period, after a 5-day grace. An invoice that is 31 to 60 days late is two periods, so the fee is 4% of the invoice amount. The fee has a minimum of 500 cents and is capped at 20% of the invoice amount.

Whenever late_fee is given an invoice that is 61 or more days late, the fee is 2% of the whole invoice amount for each started 30-day period, so 61 to 90 days late is 6%, 91 to 120 days late is 8%, and so on, not in addition to the 4%. The fee has a minimum of 500 cents and a cap of 20% of the invoice amount.
Whenever a late_fee percentage leaves a fraction of a cent, late_fee rounds half a cent up, so 4% of 12 cents is 0 and 4% of 13 cents is 1; small invoices can therefore owe no fee.
Whenever late_fee is given an invoice amount of zero or less, the fee is 0, whatever the days late.

Whenever late_fee is given a fractional days_late, it applies the same limits to the exact value (30.5 days is already in the 4% band, 60.5 days in the 6% band), and a fractional amount gives a whole-cent fee (100.5 cents at 4% gives 4).
Whenever either input to late_fee is NULL, empty text or text of any kind (even '1000' or '40'), late_fee returns NULL, even when the amount is zero or the days are negative.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given fewer than 0 points (a negative balance), it returns 'suspended'. Whenever loyalty_tier is given 0 up to 999.9 points, it returns 'bronze'; this includes 0 and 999.9.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given 1000 to 4999 points (4999.5 included), it returns 'silver'; exactly 1000 is silver.

Whenever loyalty_tier is given 20000 points or more, it returns 'platinum'. Whenever loyalty_tier is given 5000 points or more but fewer than 20000 points, it returns 'gold'; exactly 5000 is gold and exactly 20000 is platinum.
Whenever loyalty_tier is given NULL, empty text or any text (even '5000'), it returns NULL.

Whenever make_slug is given a title, it lowercases it and turns every run of characters that are not English letters a-z or digits 0-9 (spaces, punctuation, underscores, slashes, hyphens) into a single hyphen, and removes hyphens from the start and end ('  Hello,   World!! ' becomes 'hello-world').

Whenever a title contains accented or non-English letters, make_slug does not transliterate them but treats them as separators ('Café Crème' becomes 'caf-cr-me'), and a title with no a-z or digits at all, or an empty title, gives empty text.
Whenever make_slug is given a maxlen, it cuts the slug to at most that many characters and then removes any hyphen left at the end ('Hello World' with maxlen 6 gives 'hello', with 1 gives 'h').

Whenever make_slug is given a maxlen of zero or less, empty text, or text that is not a number, it returns empty text; a numeric text such as '5' works as 5 and a fractional maxlen such as 5.9 is cut down to 5.
Whenever make_slug is given a NULL maxlen, it applies no length limit; a NULL title returns NULL whatever the maxlen.
Whenever make_slug is given a number as the title, it uses the number's text (12345 becomes '12345', 1.5 becomes '1-5').

Whenever isbn_check is given exactly 9 digits, it multiplies the digits by 10, 9, 8 ... 2 from left to right, adds them, and returns the digit that brings the total to a multiple of 11; if that digit would be 10 it returns 'X'; the result is text ('030640615' gives '2', '123456789' gives 'X', '000000000' gives '0').
Whenever isbn_check is given a code with leading or trailing spaces around 9 digits, it ignores those outer spaces; spaces or hyphens inside the code make it invalid.
Whenever isbn_check is given anything other than exactly 9 ASCII digits (8 or 10 digits, letters including an X, hyphens, empty text, non-Western digits, or NULL), it returns NULL.

Whenever isbn_check is given a whole number of 9 digits (123456789), it treats it as text and works; a number with fewer digits (30640615, which has lost its leading zero) or a decimal such as 30640615.0 returns NULL, with no leading zero added.
Whenever fiscal_label is given a valid YYYY-MM-DD date, the fiscal year starts on 1 April and is named for the calendar year it ends in, so 2024-04-01 is 'FY2025-Q1' and 2025-03-31 is 'FY2025-Q4'.

Whenever fiscal_label is given a date, quarters run Q1 April-June, Q2 July-September, Q3 October-December and Q4 January-March, so 2024-06-30 is Q1, 2024-07-01 is Q2, 2024-10-01 is Q3 and 2025-01-01 is Q4; the label looks like 'FY2025-Q1'.
Whenever fiscal_label is given a date that does not exist (2024-02-30, 2023-02-29, month 13, month 00), it returns NULL, while a real leap day such as 2024-02-29 is accepted and labelled 'FY2024-Q4'.

Whenever fiscal_label is given text that is not a date in the exact form of four-digit year, two-digit month and two-digit day separated by hyphens (2024-1-5, 2024/04/01, 20240401, empty text, a number, or NULL), it returns NULL; spaces around a valid date are ignored. A valid date may also have a time of day written after it, separated by a space (such as 2026-07-01 10:30 or 2026-07-01 23:59:59). The time is ignored and the label comes from the date alone, so 2026-07-01 10:30 is 'FY2027-Q2'. A date that does not exist still returns NULL whether or not a time follows it.
Whenever fiscal_label is given an extreme year, it still applies the same rule without a range check: year 0001 gives 'FY2-Q1' with no zero padding, and 9999-12-31 gives 'FY10000-Q3'.

Whenever meeting_end is given a start time and a number of minutes, it returns the start plus those minutes as HH:MM on the 24-hour clock with zero padding ('09:00' plus 60 gives '10:00', '9:05' plus 30 gives '09:35').

Whenever a booking runs past midnight, meeting_end must never wrap around to the next day's clock time. Any meeting_end past 23:59, or exactly 24:00, gives '23:59'. For example, '23:30' plus 60 gives '23:59', 1440 minutes gives '23:59', and 1500 minutes gives '23:59'.
Whenever meeting_end is given negative minutes, it counts backwards from the start and wraps to the previous evening if needed ('10:00' minus 30 gives '09:30', '00:10' minus 30 gives '23:40').

Whenever meeting_end is given a start that is not H:MM or HH:MM with two-digit minutes (24:00, 12:60, '9am', '09:00:00', '9:5', empty text, a number, or NULL), it returns NULL; one or two digit hours and spaces around the start are accepted.
Whenever meeting_end is given NULL minutes, it returns NULL.

Whenever meeting_end is given minutes with a fraction, it drops the fraction toward zero (45.9 gives 45 minutes, -45.9 gives -45); numeric text such as '30' or '1e2' is read as a number, text that begins with a number ('30 min') uses that number, and text with no leading number or empty text counts as 0 minutes.

Whenever pct_change is given an old and a new value, it returns (new minus old) divided by the size of old, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal, as a decimal number: 100 to 150 is 50.0 and 150 to 100 is -33.3.
Whenever pct_change is given a negative old value, it divides by the old value's size without its sign, so a rise reads as positive (-100 to -50 is 50.0, -100 to 50 is 150.0).
Whenever pct_change is given an old value of 0, it returns NULL; a new value of 0 gives -100.0, and no change gives 0.0.
Whenever pct_change is given a NULL for either value, it returns NULL.

Whenever pct_change is given numeric text such as '100' or ' 100 ', it uses the number; text starting with a number ('150abc') uses the leading number; text that does not start with a number (such as 'x') or is empty is not a usable value, so pct_change returns NULL (no percentage at all) whether that text is the old value or the new value, and it is never treated as 0.
Whenever pct_change is given a binary (blob) value for either side, it returns NULL.

Whenever the pct_change result falls exactly halfway at the second decimal, it rounds away from zero (2000 to 2001 gives 0.1, 2000 to 1999 gives -0.1), but values that are only a hair below the halfway point because of decimal inexactness round down (100 to 100.05 gives 0.0).

Whenever phone_fmt is given a phone number with 10 digits, it ignores every non-digit character (brackets, hyphens, dots, spaces, plus sign, even letters or surrounding words) and returns it as (AAA) EEE-NNNN ('212.555.1234' and 'call 212-555-1234 now' both give '(212) 555-1234').

Whenever phone_fmt finds 11 digits and the first is 1, it drops that leading 1 as the country code and formats the remaining 10 ('+1 212 555 1234' gives '(212) 555-1234'); 11 digits starting with any other digit are not formatted.

Whenever phone_fmt is given anything with some other count of digits (7, 9, 12 digits, no digits, empty text, an international number like '+44 20 7946 0958', or non-Western digits), it returns the input exactly as it was given.
Whenever phone_fmt is given NULL, it returns NULL.

Whenever phone_fmt is given a whole number of 10 digits (2125551234) or 11 digits starting with 1, it formats it as text, but a number with a decimal point (2125551234.0) or one with too few digits is returned unchanged as a number.
Whenever phone_fmt is given 10 digits, it does not check that the area code or exchange is valid, so '0125551234' gives '(012) 555-1234' and '0000000000' gives '(000) 000-0000'.
Whenever avg_rating is applied to a group of rows, it returns the plain average of the ratings between 1 and 5 inclusive, with no rounding (ratings 4 and 5 give 4.5, and 5, 3, 1, 2.5 give 2.875).
Whenever a row's rating is NULL, below 1, above 5, or text (even '4'), avg_rating leaves it out of the average completely, counting neither its value nor the row.
Whenever a group has no ratings that count (no rows, all NULL, empty text, or all outside 1 to 5), avg_rating returns NULL.

Whenever avg_rating is used with GROUP BY, it gives one average per group, and without GROUP BY it averages across all selected rows; it is not available on a single value outside a group of rows (avg_rating(5) gives NULL).
Bulk prices round to the nearest 5 cents, with a 500-cent minimum order.

dg_cases.say: A customer orders minus 5 units at $1.00 each: our build accepts it and charges $0.00 (a second build rejects the order as invalid).
A customer orders 10 units at a price of $1.005 each, a half cent over $1.00: our build charges $9.55 (a second build charges $9.50, dropping the half cent).
A customer orders 10 units at $1.00 each, but the price arrives as typed text rather than a number: our build rejects the order (a second build accepts it and charges $9.50).
A customer orders 10 and a half units at $1.00 each: our build charges $9.98 for the half unit as well (a second build charges $9.50, as if the half unit were not ordered).

An order stamped 1 July 2026 at 10:30 am gets no fiscal year or quarter from our build, so it can't be filed in any period (a second build files it under fiscal year 2027, quarter 2, and does the same for dates with a time written after a space, like 23:59:59).

A catalogue code typed with stray spaces around it, like " 030640615 " from a pasted supplier list, still gets its check digit 2 from our build, which ignores the spaces (a second build gives no check digit at all and treats the entry as unusable).
Ravi's 100-dollar invoice is paid just 1 day late: our build charges no late fee (a second build charged a 2-dollar late fee, and did the same for any delay up to 30 days).
A customer with a 100-dollar credit (a negative invoice) is 31 days past due: our build charges no late fee (a second build refused to give any fee at all, treating the invoice as invalid).

An invoice of 100 dollars whose amount was entered as text rather than a number is 31 days late: our build gives no fee at all and flags the invoice as unusable (a second build accepted it and charged a 4-dollar late fee).
Priya's balance of 1000 points arrives typed as text: our build gives her no tier at all (a second build treated it as 1000 points and put her in silver).
Marcus has a blank points balance on his record: our build gives him no tier (a second build put him in bronze, the entry-level tier).
Elena's points balance was entered as the unreadable text "abc": our build gives her no tier (a second build put her in bronze).
Tom's balance of 500 points has stray spaces around it: our build gives him no tier (a second build ignored the spaces and put him in bronze).

Your page titled "Café Crème Brûlée" gets the web address "caf-cr-me-br-l-e", with the accented letters dropped and leaving broken-looking gaps (a second build wrote "cafe-creme-brulee", turning the accented letters into plain ones).
A page titled "Hello" with no length limit set still gets the web address "hello" (a second build gave no web address at all when no length limit was set).
A room booking starting at 09:00 for 30 and a half minutes is accepted and shown as ending at 09:30 in our build (a second build refuses the booking and gives no end time at all).

Priya's shop had 100 sales last month and this month's figure was typed in as the text "x" by mistake: our build reports a 100% drop, as if sales fell to nothing (a second build reports no percentage at all).
Priya's 100-rupee bill goes up to 100.05 rupees, a change of exactly 0.05%: our build reports it as 0.0% (a second build reports a 0.1% increase).
A customer enters the number 212 555 1234 with extension 5: our build leaves it exactly as typed, extension included (a second build gives no number at all, so the extension is lost along with it).
A customer enters a number one digit short, 212555123: our build keeps what they typed and shows it unformatted (a second build treats it as no valid number and shows nothing).
A customer leaves the phone field blank: our build shows a blank entry (a second build records it as no phone number at all).
A customer types their number 212-555-1234 using wide Asian-keyboard digits: our build leaves it unformatted as typed (a second build accepts it and formats it as (212) 555-1234).
